# 江村銷夏錄

**ID:** KR3h0067
**Custom ID:** ZB3h0065
**Date (file):** 2015-08-24 23:16:20.354698
**Source:** 四庫全書 文淵閣版, V826.5, p467
**Extent:** 3 卷
**Base edition:** WYG

## Authors / Editors
- 高士奇 (清朝) 撰 1645 - 1704

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A 3-*juàn* connoisseurial register by Gāo Shìqí 高士奇 (1645–1704), composed in *Kāngxī* 32 (1693, *guǐyǒu* 癸酉) during the summer months at his Pínghú 平湖 (Jiāngcūn 江村) retirement villa following his withdrawal from court office. The *xià* (summer) of the title and the explicit dating of the *yuánxù* — *Kāngxī guǐyǒu* sixth month — fix the composition to summer 1693. The book records famous calligraphies and paintings Gāo had seen at his various postings (especially during his long Kāngxī-era service in the Southern Studio with access to the inner-palace collection) and on his return to Jiāngnán. Each entry traces the piece's transmission (*kǎo qí yuánliú* 攷其源流), records the dimensions of the silk or paper, and transcribes all subsequent colophons and seal-impressions. The format is similar to Zhū Cúnlǐ's [KR3h0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3h/KR3h0044) *Tiěwǎng shānhú* and Zhāng Chǒu's [KR3h0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3h/KR3h0055) *Qīnghé shūhuà fǎng* — but Gāo's *fánlì* limits entries strictly to pieces personally eyewitnessed, sometimes adding a brief critical evaluation. *Juàn* 1–3 are the main register; the *fánlì* notes that Dǒng Qíchāng's 董其昌 calligraphy and painting were to be a separate fourth *juàn* — but this is missing in the transmitted text, perhaps never published. The Sìkù editors note that all the entries in this book are reproduced verbatim in Biàn Yǒngyù's [KR3h0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3h/KR3h0068) *Shìgǔtáng shūhuà huìkǎo* 式古堂書畫彙考 (1682), drawing on Gāo's register as a primary source. The work has two prefaces (Sòng Luò 宋犖 of Shāngqiū and Zhū Yízūn 朱彝尊 of Xiùshuǐ, both September 1693).

**Abstract**

The *Jiāngcūn xiāoxià lù* is a tightly-curated personal connoisseur's catalog of pieces eyewitnessed by Gāo Shìqí, the most prominent Kāngxī-era court connoisseur. Gāo (*zì* Dànrén 澹人, *hào* Jiāngcūn 江村, of Pínghú 平湖, 1645–1704) entered the Southern Studio under Kāngxī, advanced to *Zhānshì* 詹事, and served as one of the emperor's principal connoisseurial confidants over more than a decade. His access to the *Qiánqīnggōng* collection during this period gave him the most extensive direct exposure to the Sòng-Yuán-Míng masterpieces of any connoisseur of his generation. The 1693 composition date is unambiguous from the prefaces. The book's careful per-piece dimension-and-colophon protocol set the standard for the Qiánlóng-era imperial catalogs ([KR3h0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3h/KR3h0062) *Mìdiàn zhūlín*; [KR3h0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3h/KR3h0063) *Shíqú bǎojí*) and was directly extended by Biàn Yǒngyù in [KR3h0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3h/KR3h0068) *Shìgǔtáng shūhuà huìkǎo*. The promised Dǒng Qíchāng supplement was never published; some traditions identify it with the separately-circulated *Jiāngcūn shūhuà mù* 江村書畫目, although the relationship is contested.
